title: Launch cadence constellation & capacity-signal allocator
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Problem statement: coordinating simultaneous launches across runtime, console, and API surfaces has become a major source of friction. Teams currently operate separate cadence signals (canary windows, capacity reservations, rollback triggers) and lack a single source of truth for capacity hedging. This leads to conservative reservations, late cutovers, and manual escalation during high-concurrency launches.

Goal: design and pilot a 'constellation' model for launch cadence where a central capacity-signal allocator computes recommended reservation lanes, canary phasing, and backoff policies per cohort. The allocator should integrate telemetry (token throughput, queue depth, error rates) and produce machine-readable schedules that the Console and Runtime can consume.

Acceptance criteria:
- A spec describing the allocator's inputs/outputs and contract with Console/Runtime.
- Prototype that ingests historical telemetry and suggests lane allocations for three past launches with >= 10% reduction in peak reserved capacity without violating observed latency SLOs.
- Console UI mock and API prototype enabling teams to opt into allocator recommendations.
- Runbook for rollouts with rollback criteria and run-of-delta alerts.

Success metrics:
- 20% reduction in reserved spike capacity for pilot launches.
- Zero customer-facing SLO breaches attributable to allocator decisions in pilot.
- Adoption by at least two platform teams for the next major release window.
work_items: Draft allocator API schema (inputs: per-route QPS, latency SLO, historical KV cache hit rates; outputs: lane assignments, reserve amounts, canary windows).
Create telemetry projection job to replay last 6 months of launch spikes into the allocator prototype.
Design Console opt-in UX and decision visibility screen.
Coordinate runtime engineering on graceful enforcement hooks (soft reservation vs hard reservation).
Write rollout runbook and rollback criteria mapped to metric thresholds.
updates: 2026-02-15: Kickoff w/ runtime & console; aligned on contract shape (JSON schema v0.1).
2026-02-22: Telemetry infra spike complete — cleaned and normalized 24 months of launch events into S3 test bucket.
2026-02-28: Prototype allocator produced baseline recommendations; engineering validated enforcement hooks. Initial results show ~12% reserved reduction on two sample launches.
2026-03-05: UX review with Design — added 'explainability' panel showing which metrics drove allocation decisions (latency, queue, KV-hit).
2026-03-10: Risk review — product and SRE agreed to soft-enforcement for pilot (recommendations only) and strict monitoring; created alert playbook.
2026-03-12: PM review: green to proceed with pilot on release corridor 2026-W14 if runtime infra signoff is complete.
notes:
Trade-offs discussed: aggressive automated reservation could reduce incidents from manual underprovisioning but risks over-allocating if telemetry inputs are noisy. Decided to start with conservative smoothing and explainability surfaced to teams.

Open questions: how to prioritize lanes when multiple launches overlap and when regional availability varies; whether to expose a simple slider for 'aggressiveness' in Console; how to bill reserved capacity that the allocator recommends.
next_steps: 1) Finish schema v0.2 with runtime signoff (target 2026-03-19). 2) Run allocator against three historical launches and produce a comparison report (due 2026-03-26). 3) Build Console opt-in flow and internal pilot onboarding checklist (due 2026-03-31).
comms_plan: Pre-pilot announcement to platform teams + SRE (email + Slack #launchsquad), 1:1 onboarding with two pilot teams, weekly pilot sync, and a post-pilot readout session with metrics and lessons learned.
postmortem_plan: Collect per-launch telemetry, runbook execution logs, and stakeholder interviews; publish findings to Confluence and present at weekly platform review.
